scenario_prompt: Write a two-paragraph executive summary addressed directly to a fictional buyer's Chief Financial Officer, recommending a cloud migration. Context: a mid-market freight brokerage firm is moving its load-matching and carrier-settlement systems off on-premises Microsoft SQL Server (28 instances) running on Hyper-V (620 virtual machines) onto Google Cloud, targeting Google Compute Engine for compute and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL for the data layer, over a 2-year, $4,200,000 programme. The CFO has stated she is measured on reducing the current $1,850,000 annual technology spend and on a clean DOT compliance audit, which opens in 6 months. Cover why this matters to her now and what she should expect from the programme. Return only the summary text, two paragraphs, no headers.
text:
**Executive summary**

(Customer source material for this task is the task context itself — the CFO's stated priorities and the programme figures provided; no separate discovery notes or RFP text were supplied, so terms below are judged by the deletion test alone except where a figure is directly attributed to that context.)

You are measured on two things this year: bringing the $1,850,000 annual technology spend down, and walking into a clean DOT compliance audit that opens in six months [PF-1.13, PF-1.14: figures as stated in your programme context]. Today, that spend and that audit exposure both sit on 28 Microsoft SQL Server instances running across 620 Hyper-V virtual machines that carry your load-matching and carrier-settlement workloads [PF-1.1, PF-1.2]. We recommend moving that footprint to Google Cloud — compute on Google Compute Engine, data on Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL — so the systems the audit will examine run on infrastructure with centralized logging and usage-based billing you can inspect directly, rather than infrastructure you maintain by hand [PF-1.5, PF-1.9]. [PF-2.4 GAP: no target reduction in annual run-rate spend has been supplied — this document does not state one until a savings figure is measured or given by you.]

The programme runs two years at a proposed $4,200,000 [PF-1.13, PF-1.14: figure as stated in your programme context], and because your audit opens in month six, the first-year milestones — not the full two-year completion — are what your compliance team will be judged against. You should expect a sequenced migration of the 28 SQL Server instances and 620 VMs rather than a single cutover, with settlement-system workloads prioritized ahead of the audit window given what they support [PF-1.25: addressed to the priority you stated]. [PF-2.13 GAP: no named, verifiable proof point (a comparable migration of this scale and timeline) has been supplied for this programme — attach one before this ships, or mark it absent.] [PF-2.14 REVIEW (commitment): "settlement-system workloads prioritized ahead of the audit window" reads as a sequencing commitment — confirm this is a plan you can hold to, not a promise, before it goes to the buyer.]

## Unresolved before this document is sent

| Marker | Rule | What is needed |
|---|---|---|
| No target reduction in annual run-rate spend stated | PF-2.4 | A savings figure measured or supplied by the buyer, or confirmation none exists yet |
| No named, verifiable comparable migration attached to the programme claim | PF-2.13 | A checkable proof point (reference migration, benchmark, or prior engagement) of comparable scale/timeline |
| Sequencing of settlement workloads "ahead of the audit window" reads as a commitment | PF-2.14 | Confirmation this is a firm sequencing commitment the vendor can be held to, not an illustrative plan |
